title: Establish interlock runway and roll‑forward protocol for cross‑team PRD acceptance
creator: Riya Kapoor
description: Create an explicit interlock runway and a roll‑forward protocol that codifies how PM/Eng/Design/Legal coordinate PRD reviews, surface scope tradeoffs, and sign acceptance criteria. This ticket centralizes owners, timelines, decision gates, and a fallback plan so PRDs can move from draft -> accepted without last‑minute blocking debates.
background: Recent PRD reviews have suffered from last‑minute legal gating and undefined rollback criteria for scope reductions. That caused two delayed releases in Q4 and unclear responsibilities during canary rollouts. We need a repeatable runway with deterministic signoff lanes, an automated artifacts checklist, and a roll‑forward (partial commit) protocol for timeboxed launches.
goals: Define a 3‑stage interlock runway (Draft, Preflight, Acceptance) with owners and SLAs
Produce a single PRD Acceptance Checklist that includes legal/data residency, security, design QA, and runtime SLO gating
Design a roll‑forward protocol that describes how to commit a subset of deliverables when blockers are limited to non‑blocking scope
Automate notifications and attach artifacts (Confluence PRD, Design Figma, GitHub PR, Test Plan) to the Linear ticket
scope_in: Template for interlock runway and owners for each lane
Example runbook for roll‑forward vs rollback decisions
Onboarding docs for Legal reviewers to speed privacy/data residency signoffs
scope_out: Implementing tooling integrations for fully automated gating (separate engineering initiative)
Rewriting existing PRDs — we will provide templates and one pilot only
acceptance_criteria: Interlock runway doc published in Confluence with named owners for PM/Eng/Design/Legal and escalation contacts
PRD Acceptance Checklist exists and is linked from PRD templates
Roll‑forward protocol reviewed by Eng leads and Legal with at least one agreed example scenario (canary with feature flag) and recorded decision
Pilot PRD runs through the runway within agreed SLAs (Preflight < 5 business days) and the process retro is scheduled
decisions: Use a three‑tier acceptance tag on PRDs: MUST (non‑negotiable), SHOULD (requires mitigation plan), CAN (optional for initial ship)
Legal signoff required only for MUST items; SHOULD items must have documented mitigation and owner
Roll‑forward allowed when at most 2 CAN/SHOULD items remain and mitigation plan is attached plus a rollback trigger defined
